title: Customer sell-through stock gap: the customer report is on-hand, CIP flags the difference
acceptance_criteria: Starts only after N-0079 is closed. Do not build this during the budget ledger.
The customer report's on-hand is the stock position. CIP stores an expected position beside it and flags the gap. Neither number is rewritten to force a match.

Expected position = previous reported on-hand + inbound receipts that have a proof-of-delivery date and this customer already matched, minus units sold on this report. A shipment with no customer match stays out of the expected position.

Gap = this report's on-hand minus the expected position. A shortfall flags stock not delivered, lost, or sold outside the file. A surplus flags a receipt CIP does not have, a return, or overlapping periods.

Use the sale date when the file has one, and store that row as a day. Otherwise store the week number and year as a week. Do not invent days from a week. Fill a week-start date only when that customer's week calendar is known. A month stays a month.
Reported on-hand is required on a stock-bearing file. A sales-only file with units and no stock column is refused unless Warren names an exception before implementation.

In transit and on order are optional and stored apart from on-hand. In transit can explain a shortfall and is not added into on-hand. On order is pipeline and is excluded from on-hand and from the loss flag.
The unit gap is shown on every compared row. A highlighted flag uses a band Warren names before implementation. Do not copy the distributor 10 percent variance.
Labels that say CST are a separate later pass and are not part of this node.
